name: Delta
author: Luke "DELTA" Zelezny

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga forum, AMOS Factory downloads section, retrieved 2026-07-26. Most items there are credited "provided and archived by Lonewolf10". Archive path: Delta.
provenance.note: Documentation coverage was measured by counting how many of the library's own keyword names appear in the files shipped beside it, taking only files that can be documentation (not disk images, example programs or the library itself). That measures the DOCUMENTATION, which is what the `docs` field records; it does not set the evidence tier, which follows from what is available to read.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified unless stated in the notes. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

findings: 1.6 APPENDED to 1.4 without moving an id -- all 26 of 1.4's token entries sit at the id 1.6 gives the same keyword -- so one port serves both releases and a routine NUMBER means the same thing in each; only the addresses differ, and citations name the version they mean. The twenty 1.6 adds are mostly AmigaOS: reqtools requesters (rtEZRequestA, rtGetLongA, rtPaletteRequestA), Workbench to front and back, a public-screen lock, FindTask and RemTask, a DisplayAlert, a hard reset, and four the guide marks private -- Jsr and three Move instructions that are Poke, Doke and Loke under other names. Unlike 1.4 it HAS a data zone: six keywords take the library base from $1d8(a5), which is $f8 + 14*16 and so confirms slot 15 from the binary rather than from the guide. Its own error table is nine messages at $26d4 raised through routine 66, and THREE of them are unreachable -- nothing checks that reqtools.library opened, which is why the guide wraps every example in `If Exist("LIBS:reqtools.library")` and warns "Else you will have GURU". Delta Hard Reset loads ExecBase into a6, never uses it, and clears absolute $2a rather than $2a(a6), which is ColdCapture and the only reason to load ExecBase at all; the relocation table proves the address is literal. Delta Blit Off does not turn the blitter off, it waits for DMACONR's BBUSY, and the guide agrees with the code rather than with the name. 1.6 also fixed 1.4's string functions in passing, by moving the library to `movea.l $1d8(a5),ax / adda.w #offset,ax` -- which exposes a second defect underneath: Delta About$ is 24 bytes going into the 20 the author reserved, and in 1.6 the four that do not fit land on the first longword of Delta Decrunch. Delta Decrunch is the one keyword whose BEHAVIOUR differs between the releases, raising AMOS errors 23 and 29 in 1.4 and the extension's own two messages in 1.6 from the same two checks; the port keeps 1.4's, and modelling the difference is a pending task -- `rt.extBindings` does carry the answer for a program bound by identity, which jdprt.ts and amon.ts both read.
notes: Hardware odds and ends — drive motor, PAL/NTSC, mouse waits and decrunching.
